uplink.description: temperature report (fPort 2), D22-style two probes: probeRed 22.0 °C, probeWhite 23.0 °C, black position unpopulated
uplink._note: Synthetic LSN50v2-D22 DS18B20 frame (mode 3); cross-checked against the upstream decoder (Temp_Red 22.0, Temp_White 23.0, Temp_Black 'NULL'). Each probe is a channels[] entry carrying `temperature` (signed/10); battery and alarm stay top-level. bytes[9..10]=0xFFFF is the unconnected sentinel, so no probeBlack entry. Satisfies temperature.

uplink.description: all three probes connected (D23): probeRed 0.0 °C, probeWhite 25.2 °C, probeBlack 51.7 °C
uplink._note: TTN example "Temperature Sensor" input (reference/upstream-examples.json). Upstream oracle: BatV 2.9, Temp_Red 0, Temp_White 25.2, Temp_Black 51.7, ALARM_status FALSE. bytes[2..3]=0x0000 -> 0.0 °C (a genuine reading, not the 0xFFFF sentinel); bytes[7..8]=0x00FC=252 -> 25.2 °C; bytes[9..10]=0x0205=517 -> 51.7 °C — the third probe the pre-channels[] codec dropped.

uplink.description: only the white probe attached (red and black read the 0xFFFF sentinel)
uplink._note: Synthetic: bytes[2..3] and bytes[9..10] both read 0xFFFF, the vendor's unconnected-probe sentinel (upstream Temp_Red / Temp_Black = 'NULL'), so those positions are skipped instead of decoding as -0.1 °C; the surviving probe keeps its own label `probeWhite`.

uplink.description: no probe connected (all three words read 0xFFFF) -> error
uplink._note: Every probe word reads the sentinel: no measurement at all, so the frame is rejected rather than emitting an empty channels[].
Frame not carrying a valid temperature reading.
